cues.en: Right? One of the problems desktop has, I mean, ignoring all the purely market and getting free installs and making it just so that normal people, and by normal people, I mean obviously non-technical people will just buy a machine and it just works. One of the things that none of the distributions have ever gotten right is application packaging, right?
cues.zh: 对吧？桌面Linux的问题之一，我是说，抛开纯粹的市场问题和免费安装问题不谈，让普通人——我说的普通人显然是指非技术人员——买台机器就能直接用。所有发行版都没搞对的一件事就是应用打包，对吧？

cues.en: And now somebody will say, hey, D package is way improved and much better than RPM. And that's not at all what I'm talking about. I'm talking about actual application writers that want to make a package of their application for Linux. And I've seen this firsthand with the other project I've been involved with, which is my dialogue application, right?
cues.zh: 现在有人会说，嘿，D包已经大幅改进，比RPM好多了。这根本不是我在说的问题。我说的是真正想为Linux打包自己应用的应用开发者。我在参与的那个项目——我的对话应用——就亲身经历过这个问题，对吧？

cues.en: We make binaries for Windows and OS X. We basically don't make binaries for Linux. Why? Because making binaries for Linux desktop applications is a major fucking pain in the ass, right? You don't make binaries for Linux. You make binaries for Fedora 19, Fedora 20. Maybe there's even like, rel 5 from 10 years ago. You make
cues.zh: 我们为Windows和OS X做二进制包，基本不为Linux做二进制包。为什么？因为为Linux桌面应用做二进制包简直他妈的痛苦至极，对吧？你不是为Linux做二进制包，你是为Fedora 19、Fedora 20做二进制包，甚至可能是十年前的RHEL 5。你为

cues.en: binaries for Debian stable actually you don't make binaries for Debian stable because Debian stable has libraries that are so old that anything that was built in the last century doesn't work right but you might make binaries available for Debian whatever the code name is for unstable and and even that is a major pain because Christ we had this
cues.zh: Debian stable做二进制包——其实你根本不为Debian stable做二进制包，因为Debian stable里的库太老了，上个世纪编译出来的东西都跑不正常。但你可能为Debian unstable（不管代号是什么）提供二进制包，而且即便如此也非常痛苦，因为天哪，我们几天前

cues.en: small local flame fest just a couple of days ago, Damien has these rules that you're supposed to use shared libraries, right? And if you don't use shared libraries, getting your package in like is just painful. But using shared libraries is not an option when the libraries are
cues.zh: 刚在本地小范围吵了一架。Damien定了些规矩，说你得用共享库，对吧？如果你不用共享库，想把包弄进去简直痛苦。但当库还是实验性的、

cues.en: experimental and the libraries are used by two people and one of them is crazy so every other day some ABI breaks right so you actually want to just compile one binary and have it work preferably forever and preferably across all the Linux distributions and
cues.zh: 只有两个人用、其中一个还是疯子的时候，用共享库根本不是选项，所以隔天就有个ABI挂掉，对吧？所以你其实就想编译一个二进制包，最好能永远用下去，最好还能跨所有Linux发行版通用。

cues.en: I actually think distributions have done a horribly, horribly bad job. One of the things that I do in the kernel, and I have to fight this every single release, and I think it's sad, we have one rule in the kernel. There is one rule. We don't break user space. Everything else is kind of a guideline. The whole security thing, it's a guideline that we shouldn't do stupid shit, right?
cues.zh: 我真心觉得各发行版做得糟糕透顶。我在内核里做的一件事——每个版本我都得为此斗争——我觉得挺悲哀的：内核里只有一条规则，就一条：我们不破坏用户空间。其他一切都只能算指导原则。整个安全那套东西，也就是我们不该干蠢事，那只是个指导原则，对吧？

cues.en: But that's not a hard rule. People do stupid shit all the time. I don't get that upset. People break user space. I get really, really angry. This is something that is religious for me. You do not break user space. And even in the kernel, every single release, I have people saying, OK, I'm changing this ABI because it's cleaning stuff up. And I'm like, no, you're not changing that ABI because I will
cues.zh: 但这并不是硬性规定。人们总是会做些蠢事，我不会特别生气。人们破坏用户空间，我就会非常非常愤怒。这对我来说是一条铁律。绝不能破坏用户空间。即使是在内核里，每次发布新版本，我都会听到有人说：“好吧，我要改这个 ABI，因为这样可以清理一些东西。”我会说：不，你不能改这个 ABI，否则我就会

cues.en: crush you, right? And actually, it's often okay to exchange ABI as long as nobody notices, but immediately when somebody notices, it's a bad thing. And this is like a big deal for the kernel and I spend a lot of effort explaining to all the developers that this is a really, really important thing and then all the distributions come in and they screw it all up because they break binary compatibility left and right.
cues.zh: 把你彻底收拾掉，明白吗？实际上，只要没人注意到，改动 ABI 往往也没关系，但一旦有人注意到了，那就是坏事。这对内核来说非常重要，我花了很多精力向所有开发者解释这一点。结果各个发行版一进来，就把这一切搞砸了，因为它们到处破坏二进制兼容性。

cues.en: They update glibc and everything breaks. Hey, you can recompile everything, right? That really seems to be the mindset quite often. It's like the glibc people say, it was a bug. Look, here's the standard. It says you can't rely on that. Nobody cares. If it's a bug that people rely on, it's not a bug, it's a feature, right? And I won't even get into all the other libraries.
cues.zh: 它们更新 glibc，然后所有东西都坏了。嘿，你可以重新编译所有东西，对吧？这似乎经常就是他们的思维方式。glibc 的人会说：“这是个 bug。看，标准就在这里写着，你不能依赖它。”没人关心。如果这是人们一直依赖的 bug，那它就不是 bug，而是特性，对吧？其他库的问题我甚至都不想展开说了。

cues.en: but it's really sad when the most core library in the whole system is okay with breaking stuff and as long as things improve and they fix the ABI. So that's my rant and that's what I really fundamentally think needs to change for Linux to work on the desktop because you can't have application writers do 15 billion different versions and
cues.zh: 但当整个系统最核心的库都觉得破坏现有东西没关系，只要一切有所改进、ABI 得到修复时，这真的很令人难过。所以这就是我的牢骚，也是我认为 Linux 要在桌面上真正发挥作用，根本需要改变的地方，因为你不能让应用开发者维护 150 亿个不同版本，然后

cues.en: I'm on record as saying that maybe Valve will actually save the Linux desktop. And it's actually not because I think games are important. I don't care. I don't play games. I think some people do, so games may be important. But the really important issue is I guarantee you Valve will not make 15 different binaries. And I also guarantee you that every single desktop distribution will care about Valve binaries. So...
cues.zh: 我曾公开说过，也许 Valve 真的会拯救 Linux 桌面。其实这并不是因为我认为游戏有多重要。我不在乎，我不玩游戏。我知道有些人玩，所以游戏可能很重要。但真正重要的是，我敢保证 Valve 不会制作 15 个不同的二进制版本。我也敢保证，每个桌面发行版都会在意 Valve 的二进制文件。所以……

cues.en: The problem is Valve will build everything statically linked and create huge binaries and that's kind of sad, but it's what you have to do right now. I would like to come back to the topic of getting your application running everywhere and every distribution and compare it to the out of three modules in the kernel where the rule is to get your module in the kernel.
cues.zh: 问题是 Valve 会把所有东西都静态链接，生成巨大的二进制文件，这有点悲哀，但你现在只能这么做。我想回到让应用能在所有地方、所有发行版上运行的话题，把它和内核的树外模块作比较——那里的规则是让你的模块进入内核。

cues.en: Could we ask maybe the same for the application to get the version to distributions? I think that's what actually happens quite often. I mean, this is what most of you, actually, I don't know what most of you are doing. I'm assuming most of you maintain one or more packages. Am I completely wrong?
cues.zh: 我们能否对应用提出同样的要求：让应用进入各个发行版？我觉得这其实经常发生。我是说，你们大多数人……其实我不知道你们大多数人在做什么。我猜你们大多数人维护着一个或多个软件包。我完全错了吗？

cues.en: So most of you, your work is literally to bring in the applications into the system. And I think that's actually the right solution for all the base applications. Do not get me wrong. I do not think that something like 90% of the core stuff that is open source should just be in the distribution. But then there's the crazy stuff, right?
cues.zh: 所以你们大多数人的工作，字面上就是把应用带进系统。我认为对所有基础应用来说，这其实是正确的解决方案。别误会。我并不是说 90% 的开源核心东西都应该直接放进发行版。但还有那些疯狂的东西，对吧？

cues.en: something like some surface is open source, but let's face it. We have maybe a thousand users worldwide out of which maybe a couple of hundred are running Linux out of which maybe ten are running on Debian. I don't know. We do have some numbers, so those numbers are not completely made up, but my point is
cues.zh: 比如 Subsurface 是开源的，但面对现实吧。我们在全世界可能有一千个用户，其中也许几百个跑 Linux，其中也许十个跑 Debian。我不知道。我们确实有些数字，所以这些数字不完全是编的，但我的重点是

cues.en: If you have 10 users on Debian, and you have 10 users on Fedora, and I know we have a couple of users on... Actually, we have a couple of users on Arch, and most of the Linux users seem to be on Ubuntu, which actually kind of makes sense, right? Because divers are not necessarily computer technical people, and Ubuntu has been selling to that kind of crowd. So if you have that kind of situation,
cues.zh: 如果你在 Debian 上有 10 个用户，在 Fedora 上有 10 个用户，而且我知道我们在……其实我们在 Arch 上有几个用户，而大多数 Linux 用户似乎都在 Ubuntu 上，这其实挺合理，对吧？因为潜水员不一定是懂电脑技术的人，而 Ubuntu 一直在面向这类人群。所以如果你处于这种情况，

cues.en: Does it make sense to have people inside every distribution package that application for that distribution and do so in a really timely manner when we're making major changes that is really important to users because without those changes, their dive computer does not work, right? No, it does not make any sense at all. So even for open source projects, bringing that project into a project like Debian is just
cues.zh: 让每个发行版里的人都为该发行版打包那个应用，并且在我们做出对用户非常重要的重大变更时非常及时地跟进，这合理吗？因为如果没有那些变更，他们的潜水电脑就用不了，对吧？不，这完全不合理。所以即使是开源项目，把项目带进像 Debian 这样的项目也只是

cues.en: waste of manpower. You guys have better things to do. Trust me, you really do. Some surfaces of fun applications, but nobody should waste their life maintaining... Oh, maybe the maintainer is actually here. But the point is, I'm grateful we actually do have a Debian maintainer. Did I screw that up? No, but it's...
cues.zh: 浪费人力。你们有更好的事情要做。相信我，真的。Subsurface 是个有趣的应用程序，但没人应该把一生浪费在维护……哦，也许维护者就在现场。但重点是，我很感激我们确实有一位 Debian 维护者。我是不是说错了？没有，但这是……

cues.en: This is an example of something where it would make more sense for us. Like, for Windows, we have nightly builds. And by we, I don't mean me because I haven't touched a Windows machine in a long time. But Dirk Hondo, who is the real maintainer, builds basically nightly. And it's really convenient because these users that have problems with a particular model of die computer, he can make a Windows binary and say, hey, install that.
cues.zh: 这是一个对我们来说更有意义的例子。比如Windows，我们有每日构建。这里的“我们”不是我，因为我已经很久没碰过Windows机器了。但Dirk Hondo才是真正的维护者，他基本上每天都会构建。这非常方便，因为对于那些特定型号的潜水电脑有问题的用户，他可以做一个Windows二进制文件，然后说，嘿，安装这个

cues.en: package and see if it fixes your problem. This is what you want for real users, right? For Linux, we can't do that. The Debian package is out of date. It's not a nightly build. There's no way to create a nightly build. The only thing you can tell these kind of people is, hey, take the git tree and compile it and see if it works or not. And that works if you're people like us. But if you're a diver who's in
cues.zh: 包看看能不能解决你的问题。这才是真实用户想要的，对吧？对于Linux，我们做不到这一点。Debian包已经过时了。它不是每日构建。没办法创建每日构建。你唯一能告诉这些人的就是，嘿，拿git树编译一下看看行不行。如果你是我们这样的人，这办法行得通。但如果你是一个潜水员，

cues.en: and has traveled with his dive computer and is running Ubuntu or Debian, it's not really a very good solution, right? So even for open source, I don't think distros should maintain everything. You should do the core, and the core is still going to be thousands of packages, right? There's no question about that. And then we have all the commercial software and Debian
cues.zh: 带着潜水电脑旅行，跑的是Ubuntu或Debian，这就不是什么好方案了，对吧？所以即使对于开源，我也不认为发行版应该维护所有东西。你应该做核心部分，而核心仍然会有成千上万个包，对吧？这点毫无疑问。然后我们还有所有商业软件，而Debian

cues.en: It's probably mostly people who really don't care. I don't know. Maybe I'm just projecting here. What is Debian's feeling about, like commercial databases and stuff like that? I don't know. Yeah. So I'm probably talking to the wrong crowd, but some other distributions definitely have the whole thing with, no, hey, Valve is actually using Debian, isn't it?
cues.zh: 大概主要是那些根本不在乎的人。我不知道。也许我只是在投射自己的想法。Debian对商业数据库之类的东西是什么态度？我不知道。是啊。所以我可能是在跟错误的人群说话，但其他一些发行版肯定有整套东西，不，嘿，Valve其实在用Debian，不是吗？

cues.en: They started off using Ubuntu, but now they're using Debian. So even Debian should be aware of these kinds of commercial packages. And for them, they have to give a package. And right now, they have to pick not just a distro, but a version of the distro.
cues.zh: 他们一开始用的是 Ubuntu，但现在用的是 Debian。所以连 Debian 也应该关注这类商业软件包。对他们来说，他们必须提供一个软件包。而现在，他们不仅要选一个发行版，还要选发行版的具体版本。
